translations.text: King Josiah celebrated the Passover of the Lord in Jerusalem, and they slaughtered the Passover sacrifice of the Lord on the fourteenth day of the first month.
And he appointed and stationed the priests in the temple of the Lord according to the daily schedule, clothed in priestly robes.

And he said to the Levites who served there, “Sanctify yourselves and prepare yourselves according to the holiness of the ark of the covenant of the Lord, in the temple that King Solomon, son of David, built.

Let no uncleanness or defilement be found among you. Now perform the service of the Lord your God, and gather and prepare the whole nation of Israel, and arrange them according to the order of their ancestral heads and their tribes,

as David king of Israel and his son, the great Solomon, prescribed and wrote. Let the Levites stand in the temple, each according to the order of his ancestors, before their brothers, the children of Israel.
And according to the earlier arrangements, slaughter the Passover animals and prepare the sacrifices, and celebrate the Passover according to the Lord’s command, as he commanded through Moses.”
And Josiah generously gave the people thirty thousand lambs and young goats, and three thousand calves.

All this was given by the king’s command to the people, the priests, and the Levites. Furthermore, Hilkiah and Zechariah gave the chief priests, the leaders of the people, and the priests two thousand six hundred sheep.
And Jeconiah and Shemaiah and Nathanael, their brother, and Rabias and Uzziel and Joram, commanders of thousands, gave the Levites five thousand sheep and five hundred calves for the Passover.
And the priests received all this and prepared the Passover of Unleavened Bread magnificently, with every splendid adornment.

Arranged according to their families and the order of their ancestral divisions, the priests stood before the people to offer the Passover to the Lord, according to what was written in the law of Moses.
And thus, toward morning, they prepared the Lord’s Passover by roasting it over fire, and cooked the other raw meat with seasoning in kettles and pots,
and served it before the people. After this, the chief priests prepared for themselves and their brothers, the sons of Aaron,
because the priests were offering the fat to be burned in the fire. And the Levites prepared for themselves and their brothers, the priests, the sons of Aaron.
And the sons of Asaph, the singers of psalms, prepared themselves, as King David had appointed Asaph, Zechariah, and Eddinus.
And the gatekeepers were watchful at their respective gates, each according to his daily assignment, for they too were sons of Levi, and they prepared themselves.
And all together they performed the sacrifice of the Lord on that day.
And they offered the Passover sacrifice of the Lord on the altar according to the command of King Josiah.
And the children of Israel who were present at that time celebrated the Lord’s Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
And there had never been such a Passover in Israel, for no one had celebrated a Passover like it since the time of Samuel the prophet,
nor had any of the kings of Israel celebrated the Passover as King Josiah did, together with the priests, the Levites, the Jews, and all Israel who were living in Jerusalem at that time.
In the eighteenth year of Josiah’s reign, he celebrated that Passover.
And Josiah’s deeds were upright before the Lord his God, and he served the Lord with all his heart and mind.
And the other kings who came before him, concerning whom it is indeed written: “They sinned and acted lawlessly among all the nations, grieved the Lord, and opposed his word in Israel.”
And after all these virtuous deeds of Josiah, Pharaoh king of Egypt came to wage war at Carchemish, in the region of the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to fight against him.
And the king of Egypt sent word to him, saying, “What is there between me and you, king of Judea?”

“It is not against you that the Lord God has sent me, for I am going to fight in the region of the Euphrates. Now the Lord is with me. Do not hinder me, for the Lord urges me to go and fight in the region of the Euphrates. Stand aside from me, and do not oppose the Lord.”
Josiah did not turn his chariot back, but undertook to fight against him. He did not listen to the words of Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke to him from the mouth of the Lord.
Instead, he mustered for battle against Pharaoh on the plain of Eddaus, and the commanders came down to King Josiah.
King Josiah said to his servants, “Take me away from this battle, for I have become very weak.” His servants immediately took him away from the battle.
He climbed into his second chariot, and when he reached Jerusalem, he died and was buried with his fathers.

And all the people lamented and mourned for Josiah. Jeremiah the prophet composed laments for Josiah, and, sitting with the women, they sing Jeremiah’s laments to this day. They issued a command that throughout their generations they should continually lament him in Israel.

All this is written in the books of the history of the kingdoms of Israel: the deeds Josiah performed, his virtuous acts, his great righteousness and glory, and the wisdom of his careful observance of the laws of the Lord. The books of the kingdom of Israel and Judah recount all this down to the present day.
They took Jeconiah, the son of Josiah, from his family and made him king. Jeconiah reigned in place of his father Josiah when he was twenty-three years old.
He reigned over Judea and Jerusalem for three months. Then the king of the Egyptians forbade anyone to reign in Jerusalem.
He imposed a tribute on them of one hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
And the king of Egypt appointed Jehoiakim, the brother of Jeconiah, as their king, and Jehoiakim reigned over Judea and Jerusalem.
Jehoiakim bound the leading men and the rulers of the house of Israel, and brought his brother Zerah out of the land of the Egyptians to himself.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king over Judea and Jerusalem, and he did evil before the Lord.
In his days Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians, came up, bound him with bronze fetters, and took him to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar also took some of the vessels of the house of the Lord, carried them away, and placed them in storage in the house of his idols in Babylon.
All this concerning him, his abominations, and his lawless deeds is written in the books of the chronicles of the kings.
His son Jehoiakim, who was eighteen years old, reigned in his place.
He reigned in Jerusalem for three months and ten days, and he did evil before the Lord.
After one year Nebuchadnezzar sent for him and took him to Babylon, together with the treasure of the house of the Lord.
And he appointed Zedekiah king over Judea and Jerusalem. Zedekiah was twenty-one years old, and he reigned for eleven years.
He did evil before the Lord and did not turn away from his evil deeds. He did not listen to the words of Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke to him from the mouth of the Lord.

He did not keep the oath he had sworn to King Nebuchadnezzar in the name of the Lord. Instead, he broke his word and rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar, stiffening his neck and hardening his heart against the laws of the Lord, the God of Israel.

The leaders of the people and the priests committed many acts of wickedness and acted lawlessly. They multiplied their abominations beyond those of all the nations and defiled the Lord’s holy temple in Jerusalem.
The God of their fathers sent his messengers and prophets to them so that they would turn back, because he had compassion on them and on his holy temple.
But they despised his messengers, and on the day when the Lord spoke to them, they made jokes and mocked his prophets.
The Lord became angry with their nation, and because of their wickedness he brought the kings of the Chaldeans against them.
And they killed their young men with the sword and poured out their blood around the holy temple. They spared neither children nor virgins, neither their old people nor their young men.

But he gave all this into their hands. They took all the vessels of the house of the Lord, both large and small, the furnishings and vessels of the ark of the Lord, and all the treasures of the king of Israel, and carried them to Babylon.
And they burned down the temple of the Lord, tore down and demolished the wall of Jerusalem, and burned its towers with fire.
All its glory came to an end, and they drove the survivors before them with the sword and took them captive to Babylon.
And they became servants to them and their sons until the kings of Persia, fulfilling the word of the Lord that he had spoken through the mouth of Jeremiah the prophet.

Until the Lord was pleased with the land, he emptied it and gave it Sabbath rest. All the time it lay desolate was counted as its Sabbath rest, until seventy years were completed. In the first year of Cyrus’s reign, the seventy years of captivity for Judah and Benjamin were completed. Cyrus reigned for thirty years in all.
And in the first year of the reign of Cyrus of Persia, the word of the Lord that he had spoken through the mouth of Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled.
And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, king of Persia, and Cyrus commanded that a proclamation be announced throughout his kingdom, saying:
“Thus says Cyrus, king of Persia: The king of the whole world, the Lord God of Israel, the Most High Lord, has revealed this to me,
and has appointed me and made known to me that I should build him a temple in Jerusalem in Judea.

Now whoever there is and remains with him from among the Jewish people, may the Lord God be with him. Let him go up to Jerusalem with the Jews and build the temple of the Lord God of Israel. This is the Lord who dwells in Jerusalem.
And everyone who lives in each place shall help them with gold and silver,
and with horses and all kinds of livestock, and shall donate all their equipment to the temple of the Lord God in Jerusalem.”

And the leaders shall arise according to the clans and ancestral heads of the people of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, together with the priests and Levites and all those whose spirits the Lord stirred up to go up and build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem; and those around them
shall all help with silver and gold, horses and livestock, and shall pledge to the Lord as much as comes into their minds.
And King Cyrus had the sacred vessels of the Lord brought out, which Nebuchadnezzar had brought from Jerusalem and placed for safekeeping in the house of his idols.
Cyrus, king of Persia, had them brought out and ordered the vessels to be given to Mithridates, his treasurer.
And Mithridates counted them and gave them to Sanabassar, the administrator of Judah.

And this was the number of the vessels and furnishings of the Lord: one thousand gold vessels, one thousand silver vessels, twenty-nine silver censers, thirty gold dishes, two thousand four hundred twenty silver dishes, and one thousand other furnishings.
The total number of gold and silver furnishings that they brought was five thousand four hundred sixty-nine.
And all these were handed over to Sanabassar, and they took them and brought them from Babylon to Jerusalem, together with all the captives.

During the reign of Artaxerxes, king of Persia, those who lived around Judea and Jerusalem wrote to him: Balsamus, Mithridates, Belgius, Rathumus, Beeltethmus, Samellius the scribe, and many others with them who lived along the coast—Canaanites, Tyrians, Ammonites, Moabites, Samaritans, and many other officials. They wrote a letter in this form:

“To King Artaxerxes, our lord, from your servants Rathumus, who pays homage to you, and Samellius the scribe, and all our fellow councilors and the judges of the regions of the Syrians and Canaanites.”

Now let it be known to you, our lord and king, concerning the Jews who left you and came to us, going to Jerusalem, the rebellious and hostile city: they are rebuilding it and its public squares, and they intend to strengthen its walls and build its temple high.
Now, if they rebuild this city and finish its wall, they will pay taxes to no one, but will even stand against kings.
For they boastfully put their hope in their temple. Now it seemed good to us that you should give urgent attention to this matter,
our lord and king, and investigate and examine what your fathers and ancestors wrote.
You will find a book of records and learn that this city belongs to rebels, and its kings
and the Jews, its inhabitants, have always been rebellious and stubborn. For this reason this city was destroyed and became deserted.
Now we inform our lord and king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are raised, you will no longer have authority or passage in the regions of the Syrians and Canaanites.
Then King Artaxerxes wrote to Rathumus, Beeltethmus, Semellius the scribe, and all the others living in the regions of Samaria and of the Syrians and Canaanites who had written to him:

“I have read,” he says, “your letter which you wrote to me, and I ordered a search of the books of records. It was found that this city has opposed all kings from the beginning and throughout the ages,
and heavenly warriors [?] against all the regions lived in it. Powerful and mighty kings who lived in Jerusalem ruled and collected taxes from the regions of the Syrians and Canaanites.
Now I have ordered that these men be prevented from rebuilding the city, and you must take urgent action,
so that their wickedness may not increase further, and they may not oppose and trouble our kingdom.”
Then, after reading King Artaxerxes’ letter, Rathumus and Semellius the scribe, and many others with them, hurried to Jerusalem with horses and troops,
and prevented the Jews from building. The construction of the Lord’s temple in Jerusalem was halted until the second year of the reign of Darius, king of Persia.
King Darius held a great feast and gathered all his officials, his household servants, and all the leading men of the Medes, Persians, and Chaldeans,
and all the governors, military commanders, and provincial administrators with them, from the regions of India to the regions of Ethiopia. There were 127 governors.
They ate and drank, were satisfied, and rejoiced. When it was over, King Darius entered his chamber, climbed onto his couch, and went to sleep.
Then three young men who were his chamber attendants, while the king was asleep, stood on duty inside the chamber and kept watch over him. They began speaking to one another and said:

“Come, let each of us make a statement. Whoever makes a statement wiser and more powerful than his companions’ will receive great gifts from King Darius and will appear greater and more distinguished than everyone else.

And he shall be clothed in purple, and shall drink and eat from gold vessels, sit and sleep on golden furnishings, and ride horses with gold bridles. A crown, a fine-linen turban, shall be bound on him, and a gold necklace placed around his neck.
He will sit second to Darius on the throne because of his wisdom, and will be called a relative of Darius.”
Then each wrote his statement, and they sealed them and placed them beneath King Darius’ pillow.

They said, “When he gets up, we will give him the writing, and the king and the three great princes of Persia will judge it. Whoever’s statement is found to be wisest will receive the prize for victory.”
The first wrote, saying, “Wine is victorious and more powerful than everything.”
The second wrote, saying, “The king is victorious and more powerful than everything.”
The third wrote and said, “Women are more victorious and powerful than anything else, but truth conquers everything.”
When the king awoke, he took the writing they had given him and read it.
He sent for all the nobles of the Persians and Medes, the ministers, the commanders, the governors, and the rulers.
He sat down in the place [?], and they read the writing before everyone.
The king said, “Call the young men here, and let them explain their statements.” They were called and came before him.
Everyone said to them, “Explain to us what you have written.” The first, who had spoken about the strength of wine, began to speak.
He said this: “Men, how can wine not be powerful? It makes foolish the minds of everyone who drinks it.
It makes the minds of kings and those in distress alike, and likewise those of master and servant, rich and poor.
It changes everyone’s mind and turns it toward joy, and they never remember sorrow or any suffering.
For it fills everyone’s heart with gladness and a sense of greatness.
A man does not remember kings or rulers, and it makes him speak boastfully. When he drinks, he does not remember friends, brothers, or enemies, and often draws a sword.
When the wine wears off, he does not remember what he did.
Men, how can wine not be powerful, when it compels people to do all these things?” Having said all this, he fell silent.
The second, who had spoken about the strength of the king, began to speak.
“Men, are not human beings powerful, since they possess the sea and the dry land and everything in them?

Yet the king rules powerfully over the whole earth and its people. Whatever he says and commands, they do immediately. If he commands them to fight against one another, they do not dare disobey his word.
If he sends them to war against enemies, they go and immediately build engines, mounds, walls, and towers.
They kill and are killed, and they cannot disobey the king’s command. If they are victorious, they bring all the goods to the king.

Not only the soldiers who fight, but also the farmers who work the land, when they sow and reap, bring their produce to the king. The tax collectors, in turn, compel the country to pay taxes to the king.
The king alone is powerful and rules over everything. If he commands them to kill, they kill; if he commands them to keep people alive, they keep them alive.
If he commands them to build, they build.
If he commands them to demolish, they demolish; if he commands them to plant, they plant.
The whole land obeys the king’s authority and command. The king himself does whatever he wishes. He remains at ease, sits, eats, drinks, and goes to sleep.
All the others stand guard around him and obey his command. They do not dare go anywhere or do anything according to their own wishes, nor do they dare disobey the king’s command.
Now, men, how can the king not be powerful, when the word of his command rules so powerfully over everyone?” Having said this, he fell silent.
And the third, who spoke about the strength of women and about truth, was Zerubbabel. He began to speak and said:
“Men, if the king is great, or many other people are great, or wine is strong, who is it that has prevailed and rules over them all?
Is it not women? For women give birth to kings and to all the people who rule over sea and land.
From them they were born, and women gave birth to and raised the farmers who plant the vineyards from which wine comes.
And they are the ones who make men's clothing, and through them men are adorned and honored. It is impossible for people to exist without them.
And if they gather gold and silver and all kinds of possessions, and then see a beautiful woman,
they turn toward her and gaze at her with their mouths open, and with all their desire they love her more than gold and silver and all their possessions.
A man leaves his father and mother, who gave birth to him and raised him, and his own country, and follows his wife.
He becomes so united with her, his soul mingled with hers, that he does not remember his father or his mother or his country.
From this you ought to know that your wives rule over you, for everything you produce and labor for, you bring and give to your wives.
A man takes his sword and goes on a distant journey, whether he earns something, or robs and steals, or sails over seas and rivers,
and encounters wild beasts and travels through dark places. When he steals and plunders and passes through every hardship, he comes and brings all his earnings to his wife.
For a man loves his wife more than his father and his mother.
Many have lost their minds and fallen into slavery because of their wives.
And many have been brought to ruin, died, killed, and gone astray, falling into great sins because of women.
And now, do you not believe me? Is not this great king his own master? No one among men dares approach him.
I saw the daughter of the king's concubine sitting at the king's right hand.
She took the crown from his head and put it on her own head, and slapped the king.
At this the king did not become angry, but gazed at her with his mouth open. If she laughed, he laughed with her, and if she became sad, the king coaxed her until he restored her spirits.
So, men, how can women not be strong, when they do all these things?”

Then the king and his nobles began to look at one another. And Zerubbabel began to speak about truth and said: “Men, are not women strong? The earth is great, the heavens are high, and the sun is swift, for it runs its course through the vaulted tent of heaven and swiftly flies back to its own place in a single day.
Is not the one who made all these things great? Truly, truth is greater and stronger than them all.
The whole earth relies on truth, and the heavens bless truth. All works move and tremble before it, and there is no injustice at all in truth.
Wine is unjust, the king is unjust, women too are unjust, and all human beings are unjust. All their works are unjust, and there is no truth in them, and they perish in their injustice.
But truth stands and endures and is strong forever. It is alive and has authority forever and ever.
There is no partiality in it, and it never changes. Instead, it acts justly, and injustice and evil are rejected by it. All the works of truth are pleasing to everyone.
There is no injustice in its judgment, for truth is the strength of kings, and authority and greatness. Blessed is the Lord, the God of truth.
After saying this, he stopped speaking. Then the whole assembly shouted loudly and said, “Great is truth, victorious and mighty!”

Then the king said to him, “Ask for whatever you wish, and I will give you even more than what is written here, because you have proved wiser than everyone. You shall sit second to me on my throne and be called my kinsman.”
Then Zerubbabel said to the king, “Remember the promise you made concerning the rebuilding of Jerusalem on the day when you received your kingdom, when you said
that all the furnishings and vessels of Jerusalem should be returned there, which Cyrus had set apart and removed when he conquered Babylon. He had promised to return the vessels of the Lord.
Likewise, you too, O king, promised to rebuild the temple of the Lord, which the Edomites burned when the Chaldeans laid Judea waste.
Now I implore you, my lord and king, and ask you to grant me this great gift. For this I implore you: fulfill the promise you made to the heavenly King. Do what came from your own mouth.”

Then King Darius rose and kissed Zerubbabel. He wrote letters for him to all the provincial governors, deputies, commanders, and nobles, directing them to send him and those with him on their way to go up and rebuild Jerusalem.

He also wrote a letter to all the deputies in the regions of Syria and Phoenicia and those in the regions of Lebanon, directing them to bring cedar timber down from Lebanon to Jerusalem and rebuild the city with Zerubbabel.

He wrote concerning all the Jews in his kingdom who were setting out, and exempted them from taxes. He said to all the soldiers, nobles, deputies, and provincial governors, “Let no one approach their doors to collect taxes.”
And all the places they possess shall be exempt from taxes and free, and all the Edomites shall give up the villages and lands they hold that belong to the Jews.
For the building of the temple, twenty talents a year were to be given from the royal treasury until the temple was built.

For the altar of burnt offerings, provision was to be made every day, as written in the law, so that the seventh portions and the tithes could be offered without interruption, and another ten talents were to be given each year.
All those going up to Jerusalem were to rebuild the city and be free and exempt from taxes, both they and their families, and all the priests.
He ordered that instructions be written to provide all the supplies and the priests’ robes in which they performed the service of the Lord.
He wrote that the Levites were to be given daily provisions until the temple of the Lord was completed and Jerusalem was rebuilt.
He wrote that all those who guarded the city were to be given an inheritance of land and provisions.

He sent all the furnishings and vessels of the temple that Cyrus had set apart from Babylon. Everything Cyrus had said, Darius likewise did and fulfilled, and he had all the vessels of the Lord taken back.
When Zerubbabel left the king’s presence, he raised his hands toward heaven in the direction of Jerusalem and blessed the Lord, the King of heaven.
He said, “Victory comes from you, and wisdom comes from you. Glory belongs to you, and I am your servant.
I bless you, who have given me wisdom, and I thank you, the God of our fathers.”
He took the letters, went on his way, and entered Babylon, where he told his brothers everything.
And they blessed the God of their fathers because he had granted them freedom and given them permission
to go up and rebuild Jerusalem and the temple of the Lord, where his name was invoked. And they celebrated with great joy, with every kind of musical instrument, for seven days.

After all this, they chose the patriarchs and the leaders of the households, families, and tribes to go up to Jerusalem with their wives, sons, daughters, servants, and all their possessions and equipment.
And Darius sent a thousand horses with them so that they might reach Jerusalem safely, and with musical instruments, drums, and trumpets
and dancing and every expression of joy, he sent them off to Jerusalem.
These are the names of the men who went up to Jerusalem, according to the names of their fathers and the tribes of their clans.

Among the priests were the sons of Phinehas, son of Aaron: Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and Joiakim, who is also Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, of the family of David, of the clan of Perez, of the tribe of Judah,
who spoke words of wisdom before King Darius in the second year of his reign, in the month of Nisan, the first month.
All these were Jews who, released from captivity, went up to Jerusalem. They had been taken captive by Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and, having gone up to Jerusalem,

they settled in Judea, each in their own city. Their leaders were Zerubbabel and Jeshua, son of Jozadak. From the priestly families were Nehemiah, Zareh, Rhesa, Hananiah, Mordecai, Beelsar, Aspharas, Borsel, Rhuib, and Baanah.
These are the numbers of the patriarchs of the families and their leaders: the sons of Parosh, two thousand one hundred seventy-two; the sons of Shephatiah, four hundred seventy-two;
the sons of Arah, seven hundred seventy-six;
the sons of Nephtalem the Moabite and of the sons of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred twelve;
the sons of Elam, two thousand two hundred fifty-four; the sons of Zattu, nine hundred forty-seven; the sons of Borke, seven hundred fifty; the sons of Bani, six hundred forty-eight;
the sons of Berea, six hundred twenty-three; the sons of Arge, three thousand three hundred twenty-two;
the sons of Adonikam, six hundred seventy-seven; the sons of Bosor, two thousand six hundred six; the sons of Adin, four hundred fifty-four;
the sons of Ater-Hezekiah, ninety-two; the sons of Ilana and Zeta, sixty-seven; the sons of Azara, four hundred thirty-two;
the sons of Gerdala, six hundred thirty-two; the sons of Hananiah, one hundred twenty; the sons of Arom, three hundred twenty-three;
the sons of Arsiphur, one hundred twelve; the sons of Beter, three thousand ninety-five; the sons of Bethlehem, one hundred twenty-three;
from Netophah, fifty-seven; from Natta, one hundred fifty-eight; from Beth-azmaveth, forty-two;
from Kiriath-jearim, twenty-five; from Chephirah and Teron, seven hundred forty-eight; from Chadias and Amidia, four hundred twenty-two;
from Kimara and Gabesa, six hundred twenty-one; from Macalon, one hundred twenty-two;
from Betoliam, fifty-two; the sons of Nephis, one hundred fifty-six;
the sons of Calamol and Ono, seven hundred twenty-five;
the sons of Jericho, three hundred forty-five; the sons of Senaah, three thousand three hundred thirty-one. And the sons of the priests:
The descendants of Jeddu, son of Jeshua: nine hundred thirty-two. The descendants of Immer: one thousand fifty-two.
The descendants of Pashhur: one thousand two hundred forty-five. The descendants of Carme: one thousand seventeen.
Of the Levites, one son of Jeshua, and those of Kodogiah, Bani, and Sudiah: seventy-four.
Those of priestly descent who were psalm singers, the descendants of Asaph: one hundred forty-eight.

The gatekeepers: the descendants of Shallum, the descendants of Ater, the descendants of Talmon, the descendants of Akkub, the descendants of Ater, and the descendants of Shobai, altogether one hundred thirty-nine.

The servants of the priests: the descendants of Asipha, the descendants of Tabaoth, the descendants of Keros, the descendants of Sua, the descendants of Phaleas, the descendants of Lebana, and the descendants of Agaba,

the descendants of Acua, the descendants of Uta, the descendants of Cetab, the descendants of Agaba, the descendants of Subaim, the descendants of Astana, the descendants of Cathua, and the descendants of Gellur,

the descendants of Jabua, the descendants of Gesana, the descendants of Nora, the descendants of Aseba, the descendants of Gazera, the descendants of Okozia, the descendants of Phana, the descendants of Asasra, the descendants of Bassea, the descendants of Asana, the descendants of Maana, the descendants of Naphisa, the descendants of Acuma, the descendants of Acipha, the descendants of Assur, the descendants of Pharaca, and the descendants of Basaloth,

the descendants of Gedana, the descendants of Coutha, the descendants of Charea, the descendants of Barcus, the descendants of Sesara, the descendants of Thomai, the descendants of Nasa, and the descendants of Atipha.

The descendants of Solomon’s servants: the descendants of Sapphioth, the descendants of Pharida, the descendants of Jeeli, the descendants of Lozon, the descendants of Saela, and the descendants of Saphia,

the descendants of Hagia, the descendants of Phacarea, the descendants of Sabia, the descendants of Saroth, the descendants of Massea, the descendants of Gasaia, the descendants of Addus, the descendants of Subasa, the descendants of Apherra, the descendants of Barodis, the descendants of Sabat, and the descendants of Allon.
All the servants of the priests and the servants of Solomon: three hundred seventy-two.
These were the ones who had come up from Babylon, Tel-melah, and Thelesias; their leaders were Charathalan and Allaar.

It was not possible to count the others either, neither their fathers nor their clans that were from Israel: the descendants of Dalan, the descendants of Tuban, and the descendants of Nekodan, six hundred fifty-two.

Among the priests, those who performed priestly service were not found: the descendants of Nordiah, the descendants of Akkos, and the descendants of Jogus, who took wives for themselves from the daughters of Barzillai.

And they were called by their names, but when they were sought, they were not found in the genealogical records in their allotted section. Since they were not found in the genealogy, they were set apart and did not enter the priesthood.
Nehemiah and Attharias told them not to approach the holy things until a high priest arose who would be clothed with revelation and truth.
All Israel, from twelve years old and upward, excluding the male and female servants, numbered forty-three thousand three hundred sixty.
Their male and female servants: seven thousand three hundred thirty-five. Psalm singers and ministers: two hundred forty-five.
Camels: four hundred thirty-five. Horses: seven thousand forty-six. Mules: two hundred forty-five. Donkeys: five thousand five hundred twenty-five.
The leaders, according to their ancestral houses, came to the site of the temple of God in Jerusalem and made vows that the temple should be erected on its own site. And according to their rank,
they put into the temple treasury, to support the work, one thousand minas of gold, five thousand minas of silver, and one hundred priestly robes.

The priests, the Levites, and the people settled in Jerusalem and its surrounding places, and the psalm singers, the ministers, the gatekeepers, and all Israel settled in their villages and on their farms.
In the seventh month, all the children of Israel arose from their respective places and gathered together in the spacious place at the first gate on the eastern side.

Then Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers and the whole company of priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his brothers, took their places and prepared the altar of the Lord, the God of Israel,
to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the book of Moses, the man of God.

And they gathered and separated themselves from the other peoples of the land, and set up the altar of sacrifices in its place. Although the peoples were their enemies, all the nations of the land nevertheless helped them. They brought gifts and offerings at the appointed times, and burnt offerings to the Lord in the mornings and evenings.
They celebrated the Feast of Tabernacles, as it is written in the law of Moses, and offered the daily sacrifices as commanded.
After this they offered burnt offerings at the appointed times, including the burnt offerings for the Sabbaths and the new moons, and arranged and observed all the holy festivals
and whatever vows they made to God. From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to the Lord God, although the temple of the Lord God had not yet been built.
They gave payment to the masons and carpenters, and food for them,

and likewise to the Sidonians and Tyrians, so that they would bring cedar timber from Lebanon and transport it by ship to the harbor of Joppa, as Cyrus king of Persia had previously commanded and arranged for them.

In the second year after their coming to Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak and their brothers, the chief priests and the Levites, and all who had come out of captivity to Jerusalem began to build the temple.
They laid the foundation of the house of the Lord God on the first day of the second month, in the second year after their coming to Judea and Jerusalem,

and appointed the Levites twenty years old and above to the work of serving the Lord. Jeshua and his sons and brothers, and Kadmiel his brother, and the sons of Jebuhema Babun [?], and the sons of Joda son of Iliadun, together with their brothers, took their places. All the Levites worked together on the house of the Lord, and the masons and builders built the house of the Lord.
The chief priests took their places, dressed in long robes, with musical instruments and trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, held the cymbals.
With songs they sang psalms and praised God, as David king of Israel had prescribed the songs accompanied by musical instruments.
They loudly praised and gave thanks to the Lord God, because God's goodness and glory endure forever throughout all Israel.
All the people loudly blew their trumpets and shouted with a mighty voice, praising the Lord who had established his holy temple.
The chief priests and Levites came in, those who were elders and leaders of their ancestral families, who had seen the temple before this building.
And with a loud voice and weeping, and with many trumpets and great joy,
so that the multitude could not hear the sound of the trumpets because of the sound of the people's weeping, although many were blowing the trumpets, whose sound carried even to distant places.
The enemies of the people of Judah and Benjamin heard the sound and came to see and find out what the sound of the trumpets meant.
They learned that those who had come out of captivity in Babylon were building the temple of the Lord, the God of Israel.
They approached Zerubbabel and Jeshua son of Jozadak and the other leaders of the ancestral families and said to them, “Let us also build the temple of the Lord with you.”
“Like you, we too will obey the Lord your God, for we too have longed for your departure since the day when Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians, took us captive and brought us to settle here.”
Zerubbabel and Jeshua son of Jozadak and the other leaders of Israel's ancestral families said to them, “It is not fitting for us and you to build the house of the Lord our God together.
We alone will build the temple of the Lord God, as Cyrus king of Persia commanded us.”
For these were the peoples allied with the enemies of Judah who obstructed the building.
In the time of King Cyrus, he commanded that the temple be built during his lifetime. After his death, they stopped the work for twelve years, until the second year of Darius.
And in the second year of King Darius, Haggai and Zechariah prophesied. They prophesied in Judea and Jerusalem in the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak began to build the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem, together with the prophets of the Lord, who helped them.
At that time Sisinnes, the governors of the regions of Syria and Phoenicia, Sathrabuzanes, and their other companions came to them.
They said to them, “By whose command are you building this temple and its porticoes? And who are those who intend to build and complete it?”
And the Lord's gracious care came upon the priests and the people of Judea.
They did not prevent them from building while they wrote to King Darius and waited to receive a command from him. The letter that they wrote and sent to King Darius:
“Sisinnes, governor of Syria and Phoenicia, Sathrabuzanes, and their companions, the officials and leaders of Syria and Phoenicia, to King Darius: Greetings.

“Let it be known to you, our lord the king, that we traveled to the land of Judea and entered the city of Jerusalem. There we found those who had returned from captivity and their chief priests in the city of Jerusalem, and we saw that they were building the great temple of the Lord.”
And they built with remarkable, large hewn stones, and fastened wooden beams within the wall.
The work proceeded with great speed and success in their hands, and they intend to complete it quickly and with great splendor.
Then we questioned the elders, saying, ‘By whose command are you building this house, and at whose word are you laying its foundations?’
We questioned them so that we could inform you, identify their leaders for you, and write down the names of those in charge of their work.
They answered us, saying, ‘We are servants of the Lord God, who made heaven and earth.
This temple was built many years ago by the great and powerful king of Israel.

When our fathers provoked and sinned against the Lord God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, he delivered them into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians, who was king of the Chaldeans.
In the first year of Cyrus's reign in Babylon, King Cyrus issued a written command to build this temple.

And all the gold and silver furnishings and vessels of the temple, which King Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the Lord's temple in Jerusalem and placed in storage in the house of his idols, Cyrus took back from the house of the Babylonians' idols and gave to Zerubbabel and Sanabassar.
He commanded them to bring the furnishings and vessels and place them in the Lord's temple in Jerusalem, and he commanded that this temple of the Lord be built on its own site.
Then Sanabassar went up to Jerusalem and laid the foundations of this temple. From that time until now we have been building, and it is still not completed.’
Now therefore, our lord and King Darius, order a search and look in the archives, where the records are kept in King Cyrus's treasury.
See whether they are to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem by King Cyrus's command and at his word. When you have examined King Cyrus's commands, inform us about this entire matter.”

At that time King Darius commanded a search to be made in the royal archives in Babylon. A record was found at Ecbatana [?], in the land of Media, in the place where the records were kept. It was written as follows:
“In the first year of Cyrus's reign, King Cyrus commanded that the house of the Lord be built in Jerusalem, where sacrifices are offered publicly by fire.”

And he ordered it to be built according to this design: sixty cubits high and sixty cubits wide, with three courses of hewn stone and one course of new timber. He ordered the expenses to be paid from the royal treasury.

And King Cyrus ordered the gold and silver vessels used in the house of the Lord, which Nebuchadnezzar had brought to Babylon from the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem, to be taken to the house of the Lord in Jerusalem and placed there as they had been before.

King Darius added this further command, saying: “Sisinnes, governor of all the Syrians and Phoenicians, and Sathrabuzanes, and your other companions appointed to administer Syria and Phoenicia, keep away from that place. Do not approach the Lord’s servant Zerubbabel, governor of the Jews, or the Jewish high priests, who are together building the house of the Lord on its own site.
And I have ordered that it be built in its entirety, and I will assist the Jews who went up to Jerusalem until they complete the temple of the Lord their God.

And I have issued a command that funds from the taxes of your regions of Syria and Phoenicia be given to these men to support the sacrifices to the Lord. Let Zerubbabel the governor receive bulls, rams, and lambs,

and likewise wheat, salt, wine, and oil. Let all these things be provided year after year, for as long as the priests in Jerusalem direct, for the Lord’s expenses. Let them be given day by day without interruption,
so that they may offer sacrifices to the Lord, the Most High God, for the king and his forces, and pray for the king’s life.

And I have ordered that anyone who is negligent or violates the command I have written be punished and forfeit everything he owns. Let him be hanged and tortured, and let all his possessions be taken into the royal treasury,

for where the name of the Lord has been invoked, there all the provisions of the kingdom and the nations have been commanded [?]; and he dared to intervene and obstruct, and plotted evil against the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem.
I, King Darius, have ordered that all this be carried out and completed with great care.”

Then Sisinnes, the chief governor of the regions of Syria and Phoenicia, and Sathrabuzanes and their other companions, who had been obstructing the work on the temple, received the command from King Darius
and began to oversee and attend to the work. They became fellow workers with the elders of the Jews and the high priests,
and the work on the temple prospered, because Haggai and Zechariah were prophesying.
And the temple was completed according to the command of the Lord, the God of Israel, and according to the command and will of Cyrus and Darius, in the sixth year of King Darius.
The holy temple was completed on the twentieth day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of Darius’s reign.
And the people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and all those who had come out of captivity acted as prescribed and commanded in the book of the law of Moses.
And for the dedication of the house of the Lord they offered one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs,
and twelve young goats for the sins of all Israel, according to the number of the tribes of the leaders of Israel.

And the priests and Levites were appointed according to their families, clothed in full-length robes before the Lord, the God of Israel, according to the commands in the book of Moses; and the gatekeepers were appointed to their respective gates.
And the people of Israel who had come out of captivity celebrated the Lord’s Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, for the priests and Levites had purified themselves together,
and all those who had come out of captivity, and the Levites who had been purified.
They slaughtered the Lord’s Passover sacrifice for all the Israelites who had come out of captivity, for their brothers, for themselves, and for the priests.
And the Israelites who had come out of captivity ate—all those who had separated themselves from the impurities of the Gentiles and who sought the Lord God.
They celebrated the Passover feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days and rejoiced before the Lord,
because the Lord had turned the intention of the king of the Assyrians toward them and strengthened their hands for the work of the Lord God of Israel.
When all this had happened and been completed, King Artaxerxes reigned over the Persians. Ezra went to him, the son of Azariah, son of Ezeriah, descended from Hilkiah, from Shallum,
from Zadok, from Ahitub, from Amareth [?], from Jagek [?], from Meremoth, from Zerahiah, from Savias, from Bukki, from Abishua, from Phinehas, from Eleazar, and from Aaron, the first priest.
This Ezra, who came up from Babylon, was a skilled scribe in the laws of Moses given by the God of Israel.
The king gave him great glory, and, having found favor before him, he was honored with great distinction.
Some of the Israelites went up with him to Jerusalem, along with priests, Levites, ministers who sang psalms, gatekeepers, and servants of the priests.
In the seventh year of the reign of King Artaxerxes, in the fifth month—which was the king’s seventh year—having left Babylon on the first day of the first month, on the first day of the fifth month
he entered Jerusalem, as the Lord had made his journey successful.
For Ezra was filled with all wisdom and lacked nothing concerning any of the Lord’s commandments. In accordance with the Lord’s laws, he taught Israel all the judgments and ordinances.
A written decree from King Artaxerxes reached Ezra, the priest and scribe of the law of the Lord, and it was written as follows:
King Artaxerxes, to Ezra the priest and expounder of the Lord’s laws: Greetings.

Having weighed all my benevolent intentions, I have commanded that all the people of Judea who wish to go up to Jerusalem, as well as the chief priests and Levites, be free to go with you to Jerusalem.
And in accordance with their eager desire to reach Judea and Jerusalem, I and my seven counselors have commanded
that they go and carry out everything according to the laws.

“And they shall offer sacrifices to the Lord, the God of Israel, as I and my friends vowed in Jerusalem. With all the gold and silver that may be found in the land of the Babylonians, they shall offer sacrifices to the Lord God in Jerusalem.”
And, receiving assistance from the land of the Babylonians, let the priests of the Lord God take to Jerusalem gold and silver, bulls, rams, lambs, and all the other sacrificial offerings,
and offer them on the altar of the Lord God in Jerusalem.
And whatever you and your brothers wish to do concerning the gold and silver of the tribute, do it according to the will of the Lord your God.
And the priestly equipment and the vessels of the Lord were taken to Jerusalem.
Act according to the needs of the temple of the Lord God, and place everything before the Lord your God in Jerusalem.
And let them place any other surplus and remainder, whatever there may be for the needs of the temple, in the royal treasuries.

And I, King Artaxerxes, have commanded the treasurers in Assyria and in the regions of the Canaanites: Whatever Ezra the priest and expounder of the laws of the Lord God Most High wishes to receive, give it to him without hindrance—one hundred talents of silver, according to this same rule,
and one hundred cors of wheat, and the same amount of wine and oil.
And let them receive everything according to the laws and carry it out for the Lord God Most High, so that there may be no wrath from God upon my kingdom and my son.
And a command has been given concerning you priests and Levites, ministers who sing psalms, gatekeepers, servants of the priests, and attendants of the Lord’s house.
Let no one dare to demand any taxes or anything else from them at all.
And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom given to you by God, appoint overseers and judges to judge everyone in the regions of Syria and Phoenicia who has learned the law of the Lord your God.

Teach those who do not know it. And concerning everyone who transgresses the laws of the Lord your God and the laws of our kings, you have been given authority to punish and torture them, and, if they deserve death, to kill them, or, if they deserve punishment, to punish them and exact fines.
And Ezra, the scribe of the Lord’s law, said, “Blessed is the Lord, the God of our fathers, who put all this into the king’s heart, to glorify the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem,
and greatly honored me before the king and before all his counselors, friends, and nobles.
And I was greatly encouraged by the help of the Lord my God.” And he gathered all the men of Israel who had gone up with him to Jerusalem.
These are the leaders, according to their ancestral houses and the divisions of their tribes, who went up with Ezra from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes.
Of the descendants of Phinehas, Gershon; of the descendants of Ithamar, Gamael; of the descendants of David, Perez.
Of the descendants of Phoros, Zechariah, and with him 150 men who had been taken captive.
Of the descendants of Phaath-moab, Elijah, Onias, Zerah [?], and with him 200 men.
Of the descendants of Zathses, Jezonias son of Jethel, and with him 300 men.
Of the descendants of Adinoba, [?] son of Jonathan, and with him 350 men; of the descendants of Elamese, Godoliah, and with him 70 men.
Of the descendants of Shephatiah, Zechariah son of Michael, and with him 70 men.
Of the descendants of Joab, Abadiser son of Jezel, and with him 212 men.
Of the descendants of Bani, Assalimoth son of Josaphias, and with him 160 men.
Of the descendants of Beer, Zechariah son of Berea, and with him 28 men.
Of the descendants of Astath, John son of Hakkatan, and with him 110 men.
Of the descendants of Adonikam, Esphata [?]; and these are their names: Eliphalet, Jeuel, and Semaiah, and with them 70 men. Of the descendants of Bani, Uthai son of Istalcurus, and with him 70 men.
And having gathered them on the bank of the river called Theras, and having camped there for three days, I counted them all.
None of the descendants of the priests or the descendants of the Levites was found among them.
And I sent to Eleazar, and Semaiah, Joribon, Nathan, Ennathan, Zechariah, and Mosollabon came to me—these leaders and teachers of the law.
And I told them to go to Loddeus, the chief of the treasurers.
And I instructed them to tell Loddeus and his brothers and everyone in the place of the treasurers to send us some of the priests of the house of the Lord.

And they brought us men who were mighty according to the word of the Lord and knowledgeable in the laws of the Lord, from the descendants of Mahli, who was descended from Levi and Israel: Aserevan, his sons, and his brothers, eighteen in all;
and Asebias, Annunon, and Osetan his brother, from the descendants of Chanuniah, and his sons, twenty men.
And twenty of the priests’ servants, whom David the ruler had assigned to the work of serving the Levites, whose names were recorded among the notable men.
And there we proclaimed a fast and offered prayers before the Lord our God, asking for an easy and successful journey for ourselves, our children, and everything we had with us.
For we felt reluctant to ask the king for infantry and cavalry to escort us and protect us from those who opposed us.
For we had told the king, “The power of the Lord our God is with us and with all who seek him.”
And for all these reasons we proclaimed a fast and made petitions, so that the Lord would protect us and give us success on a peaceful journey.
And we selected twelve men from the heads of the priestly families, along with Esebias and Asamias and ten of their brothers.

And we weighed out and handed over to them the silver, the gold, and the articles for priestly service belonging to the furnishings of the Lord’s house, which the king, his counselors, the officials, and all Israel had given us.
And I weighed out and handed over to them six hundred and fifty talents of silver, silver utensils weighing one hundred talents, and one hundred talents of gold,
and twenty other gold articles, and twelve articles of pure, clean bronze with the appearance of gold.

And I said to them, “You are consecrated to the Lord, and all these utensils are holy to the Lord, as are the gold and silver articles. Pray to the Lord, and may the Lord, the God of our ancestors, keep them safe and bring them in peace to his holy place.
Stay alert and guard them until you arrive and deliver them to the chief priests and Levites and to the heads of Israel’s ancestral families who are in Jerusalem,
so that the guardians of the Lord’s temple, the chief priests, and the Levites may receive the silver, the gold, and these articles for service and carry them into the Lord’s temple in Jerusalem.”

And we set out from the river Theras on the twelfth day of the first month and arrived in Jerusalem, protected by the uplifted and mighty hand of the Lord. The Lord our God delivered us from all our enemies, and we reached Jerusalem safe and in peace.

And after we had rested for three days in Jerusalem, on the fourth day we weighed out and handed over the silver and gold in the house of the Lord our God to Meremoth the priest, son of Uriah, and those who were with him:
Eleazar son of Phinehas, Jozabad son of Jeshua, Moeth son of Sabannus, and other Levites, to whom we handed everything over by weight and number.
And the weight and number were recorded that day.
And those who had come up with me from captivity among the Babylonians offered sacrifices to the Lord, the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety rams,
seventy-two lambs, and twelve male goats for deliverance. They offered all these sacrifices before the Lord, the God of Israel.
And they delivered the king’s written orders to the king’s officers, the rulers, and the governors of Syria and Phoenicia, and our nation and the Lord’s temple were honored with great distinction.

And when all this was completed, the family heads and leaders of the children of Israel came before me and said, “The whole nation of the children of Israel, together with their leaders, the priests, and the Levites, has failed to keep itself separate.
They have mingled with the pagans and foreigners and with the abominations of all the unbelievers—with the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Moabites, Ammonites, Girgashites, and Edomites.

For they themselves and their sons married their daughters, and their holy offspring became mixed with the foreign peoples, the pagans of the land. The rulers and leading men each took this lawlessness upon themselves, for they were the leaders in this evil mixing.
And when I heard these words, I tore my clothes, lamented, pulled out the hair of my head and beard, and sat in deep mourning and sorrow.

And everyone gathered around me when they heard my laments concerning the Lord, the God of Israel, and saw what I had done because of their lawlessness. For I sat there grieving until evening, when the time for the evening sacrifices arrived.
And rising from my mourning, with my clothes thus torn, I bowed down with lamentations. I raised my hands to the Lord God and cried out,
and said, “Lord, we are ashamed and tremble before your face,
for our sins have multiplied beyond our heads, and our lawless deeds have risen higher than the heavens.
From the years and times of our fathers until this day, we have been in great sin.

And because of our sins and our fathers’ transgressions, we were handed over into captivity, together with our brothers, our kings, and our high priests. All the kings of the earth put us to the edge of the sword, took us captive, and devastated our dwelling places, and we have been put to shame to this very day.
And now, how great has been your mercy toward us, Lord, in leaving a root, offspring, and a name in this place, in your holiness.
You revealed light in the temple of the Lord our God and gave us food during our servitude.
Even in captivity you did not let us slip from your hands, but became our helper, Lord, and granted us favor before the king of Persia. He honored us and supplied us with every provision.
He glorified the temple of the Lord our God, raised it up, rebuilt the desolate places of Zion, and established us in Judea and Jerusalem.
And now, what answer shall we give before you, Lord, concerning all this? For we have transgressed your laws and your commands, Lord, which you gave through your servants the prophets,
saying, ‘The land you will enter to possess is a land defiled by the defilements of the nations of that land, and their abominations have filled it.
Therefore, do not take wives for your sons from their daughters, and do not give your daughters to their sons.
Do not seek to make peace with them at any time, and you will be strong enough to eat the good things of the land, and your sons will inherit that land forever.’
And whatever troubles befell us at any time because of our deeds and because of the wickedness of our sins.

But you, Lord, full of compassion, forgave our sins and gave us such offspring and a root. Yet we again turned aside to transgress your laws and mingled with the abominations of the pagans of this land.
And you did not become angry with us so as to destroy us until no root, offspring, or name of ours remained.
Lord God of Israel, you are righteous and true. You did not wipe out our offspring, but we have remained as offspring and a root to this day.
And now, here we are today before you in our lawlessness, and we can no longer stand before your face, for our lawless deeds and evils have multiplied beyond our heads.”

And while Ezra was praying with these confessions and great lamentations, he lay face down on the ground before the temple of the Lord. All who were in Jerusalem gathered around him, great crowds of men and women, young men and virgins, for there was great lamentation among the multitude.
And Jeconiah son of Jeelus, one of the Israelites, called out and said to Ezra, “We have sinned against the Lord God and have taken wives from the foreign peoples of this land.
Even now, lawlessness remains among us. Come, all of us, let us swear an oath before the Lord and send away the wives we have taken from foreign peoples, together with their children,
as the law of the Lord our God commands. Rise quickly and carry this out,
for all our affairs are in your hands, and we are with you. Whatever you command, we will do.”
Then Ezra rose and made the leaders of the families of the priests and Levites, and all Israel, swear to act in this way. And they swore.
Then Ezra rose from the portico of the Lord’s temple and went to the house of Johanan son of Eliashib.
He stayed there, tasted no bread, and drank no water, mourning over the lawlessness and the many great sins of the multitude.
A proclamation was issued throughout Judea and Jerusalem that all who had returned from captivity should come and assemble in Jerusalem.

Those who did not arrive there within two or three days would, by the judgment of the leaders and elders, have their possessions confiscated and be excluded and expelled from the community of those who had returned from captivity.
All those of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin assembled in Jerusalem within three days, in the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month.
The whole multitude sat with him in the broad space of the portico of the Lord’s house, shivering and trembling because of the winter cold.
Ezra rose and said to them, “You are the ones who have sinned and taken wives from the daughters of foreign peoples, adding to Israel’s lawlessness.
Now make confession and give glory to the Lord, the God of our fathers.
Do his will, and separate yourselves from all the heathen peoples of the land and from the foreign wives you have taken.”
The whole multitude cried out together in a loud voice and said, “We will do just as you have said.

But it is winter, and we are a very great multitude, and we cannot endure the hardship of these conditions like this. Nor is this a task for one day or two, for we have sinned very gravely in this matter.
So let rulers and leaders be appointed over this multitude, and whenever anyone has a foreign wife in his house,
let them go and arrange a time with him. Let the elders and judges of each place be present, and let them turn away and appease the Lord’s anger against us for these great evils we have committed.”
Jonathan son of Asahel and Hezekiah son of Thocanus undertook to do this, together with Meshullam, Levi, and Shabbethai, who joined them.
They acted in every respect as those who had returned from captivity commanded.
Ezra selected men who were priests, leaders, and heads of ancestral families, each by name. They sat down on the first day of the tenth month to settle the matter.
They gathered and brought in the men and women who had foreign spouses, continuing until the first month.
Among the priests who had assembled, some were found who had foreign wives and had become involved in ungodliness.
From the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak and of his brother: Matthelas, Eleazar, Jarib, and Joadanus.
They began to send away their foreign wives, and each offered a ram for the forgiveness of the sins they had committed in ignorance.
And from the sons of Emmer: Ananias, Baddaeus, Manas, Samaeas, Hieriel, and Azarias.
And from the sons of Pashhur: Elianas, Massias, Ishmael, Nathanael, Scethledus, and Salthus.
And from the sons of the Levites: Jozabdus, Semeis, Conus, who is Salitas, Patheas, who is also Judas, and Jonas.
From the ministers who sang psalms: Eliashib and Bacchurus.
From the gatekeepers: Saloimus and Tolbanes.
And from Israel, from the sons of Parosh: Hieramas, Jeddias, Melchias, Miales, Eleazar, Asabias, and Baneas.
And from the sons of Eliakim: Mattanias, Zacharias, Jezoriel, Obadiah, Jeremoth, and Aedias.
And from the sons of Zathom: Eliadas, Eliasimus, Othonias, Arimoth, Sabbatus, and Zargeas.
And from the sons of Bebai: John, Ananias, Jozabdus, and Emathus.
And from the sons of Mani: Gamos, Samumus, Jedeus, Jasubus, Jasaelus, and Jeremoth.
And from the sons of Addi: Nathus, Moossias, Lacunus, Naidas, Mattathias, Esthel, Balunus, and Manasseh.
And from the sons of Annas: Elionas, Asseas, Melchias, Sabbeus, Simon, and Chosameus.
And from the sons of Asomath: Anneus, Mattathias, Baneus, Eliphalat, Manasseh, and Shimei.

And from the sons of Baani: Jeremiah, Momdius, Ismaerus, Joel, Mamde, Pedias, Anos, Rabasion, Anasibus, Mamnitanaemus, Eliasis, Banus, Eliali, Someia, Shelemiah, and Nathanias. And from the sons of Ezora: Aem, Ezriel, Azael, Samatus, Zambri, and Joseph.
And from the sons of Naum: Zazikeas, Labadias, Edesiuel, and Benesias.
All these were men who had married foreign women, and they sent away their wives and their children.
And the priests, the Levites, and those from Israel settled in Jerusalem and in the countryside on the first day of the fifth month, and the children of Israel settled in their own dwellings.
And the whole multitude gathered together with one accord in the open area on the eastern side, before the gate of the temple.
And they told Ezra, the high priest and scribe of the law, to bring the law of Moses, which had been given by the Lord, the God of Israel.
And Ezra brought the law into their midst, before all the men and women and before all the priests. And they heard the law of the Lord on the first day of the seventh month.
And he read in the open area before the gate of the temple, from morning until midday, before all the men and women. And the whole multitude listened to and understood the law of the Lord God.
And Ezra, the priest and scribe of the law of the Lord, stood on a wooden platform that had been prepared.
And beside him on his right stood Mattathias, Samus, Ananias, Azarias, Uriah, Hezekiah, and Baalsamus.
And on his left stood Phalteus, Mishael, Melchias, Lothas, Ubus, Nabarias, and Zacharias.
And Ezra took the book of the law in his hand, for he was seated in great honor before everyone, and the whole multitude sat before him.
And when he opened the book of the law, the whole multitude stood up, and Ezra blessed the Lord God Most High, the God of hosts and the Almighty.
And the whole multitude said together, “Amen.” They raised their hands, fell to the ground on their faces, and worshiped the Lord God.
And Jeshua, Annus, Sarabias, Adinus, Jacubus, Sabateas, Audeas, Manneas, Calitas, Azariah, Jozabdus, Hananiah, and Phigathos.
These were the Levites who taught the people the laws of the Lord and enabled them to understand, and they were filled with the laws of the Lord God.
And Attharates spoke to Ezra, the priest and expounder of the Lord’s law, and to the Levites who were teaching the multitude.
He said to them before everyone, “This day is a holy day to the Lord.” And they were all overcome with grief as they heard the Lord’s law.
“Go, eat rich food and drink sweet drink, and send rich food to those who have nothing,
for this day is holy to the Lord. Do not make it sorrowful, for it is the Lord God who has glorified us.”
And all the Levites instructed the multitude, saying, “This day is holy; do not make it sorrowful.”

And they said to the multitude, “Let whoever has anything eat and drink and be glad, and give to whoever has nothing. Let everyone be very glad today, for you have been filled and have understood the words of the Lord’s law, for which you gathered and which we taught you.”
